scenes.headline: How a phone scan becomes a splat room
scenes.sub: Echo-3, read from its public files
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pane! Let's see how a phone walk around a room becomes a Gaussian splat scene.

scenes.text: Echo-3 builds the scene from what the phone captured, then fills the regions it missed to match their surroundings.
scenes.say: Echo-3 keeps what the phone saw, then fills in the places it missed so they match the rest.

scenes.title: From a walkthrough to a web viewer

steps.say: The phone saves the scan, then uploads it for cloud processing.
Out comes a splat scene in the SPZ format.
The viewer streams it as three levels of detail.
A small occupancy grid and the viewer let you walk through.

scenes.title: One splat in the SPZ file

steps.say: Each splat is a position, an opacity and one colour.
Then a scale and a rotation. Twenty bytes raw, about sixteen once compressed.

scenes.label: of splats are flat discs, thin axis at the format floor

scenes.text: The output format is open and readable; the model, its training data and its accuracy are not.
scenes.say: The file is open and you can read it. The model behind it is closed.
A phone scan goes in, flat discs come out, and the model stays closed.
